topic_gaps.reason: Does not exist in Washington as a wage-withholding regime. Washington levies no personal income tax, so there is no state income tax withholding statute and no state counterpart to federal wage withholding under 26 U.S.C. ch. 24 (s 3401 et seq.), which is the operative law for a Washington employee. The only state tax imposed on an individual's income is the capital gains excise tax, chapter 82.87 RCW, which I did verify on the register (fetched https://app.leg.wa.gov/RCW/default.aspx?cite=82.87, HTTP 200, breadcrumb 'Home / State laws and rules / RCWs / Title 82 / Chapter 82.87', heading 'Chapter 82.87 RCW - CAPITAL GAINS TAX'): it is self-assessed and self-reported by the individual with no employer withholding, so it does not answer this topic. The payroll deductions that do exist in Washington are contributions rather than income tax withholding: Paid Family and Medical Leave premiums under chapter 50A.10 RCW and long-term services and supports premiums under chapter 50B.04 RCW.

No CAPTCHA and no 403 as such, and no attempt was made to evade the redirect. Because in-force status cannot be established from a secondary source, Justia, FindLaw, Casetext and agency pages were deliberately NOT used as substitutes. licence.summary: NOT VERIFIED. The West Virginia Code site's own copyright or terms page could not be read, because code.wvlegislature.gov redirects this network to fbi.gov, so nothing here rests on the register's own words. As a matter of law rather than observation: under the US government edicts doctrine (Georgia v. Public.Resource.Org, 590 U.S. 255 (2020)) the text of the West Virginia Code as enacted is not copyrightable, so reuse and adaptation of the statutory text itself would be lawful whatever the site asserts. Two things a human must check on the register once it is reachable: (a) the official annotated West Virginia Code is published under contract by a commercial publisher (historically Michie/LexisNexis), so annotations, notes and arrangement in a print or Lexis volume are the publisher's and must not be reused; and (b) whether the Legislature's own site asserts copyright over the free online version, as Washington's does. open_licence is recorded as false because it could not be confirmed, NOT because a restriction was found.
